title: Auditory Illusions
idiom: Bridget Riley-like op-art screenprint, an ear that exists only where the waves bend
hero_prompt: Op-art screenprint in the manner of Bridget Riley, black and white with one band of warm red, hand-made on paper, flat and graphic with visible ink texture, not a photograph, not a 3D render, no depth-of-field, wide panoramic composition: the whole field filled with even parallel wavy black lines on white; in the centre, half the height of the frame, the clear shape of a large human ear seen from the side, made only of lines: inside the ear's shape the lines curve into nested bands that follow the ear's outer rim, its inner fold and its lobe, then curl into a tight spiral at the ear's opening, while outside it the lines run on as level waves; the ear is easy to recognise, with no outline drawn around it and no solid black areas anywhere. One horizontal band of warm red wavy lines runs through the field behind the ear. Crisp, optical, flat, mostly white.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on a warm red ground, no shading or gradients: a bold human ear seen from the side, its inner curl cut as one thick spiral. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
